args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 failed production health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate following its deployment. As the most recent production-healthy release, v2.3.0 was rolled back to across all production regions. Rollback completed and verified: all regions now run v2.3.0, service is healthy, and error rate dropped to 0.2%. Root cause of the v2.3.1 failure is under investigation.
args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what happened:

1. **Diagnosis**: The latest deploy of `checkout-api` (v2.3.1) was failing health checks in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. The most recent release that was healthy in production was **v2.3.0**.
2. **Rollback**: Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0. Verified afterward: service is healthy in all regions, error rate down to 0.2%.
3. **Incident**: Opened a SEV2 incident (**INC-0001**), which paged the on-call engineer, describing the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback to v2.3.0, and the verified recovery.

transcript.reasoning_content: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0. Rollback to v2.3.0, then create SEV2 incident. Rollback depends on knowing the version (already known), incident doesn't depend on rollback result technically, but better to describe what happened — do rollback first, then incident. Actually incident summary can be written independently, but ordering safer: rollback then incident. Could do both in parallel since incident text is known. But if rollback fails, incident description would be wrong. Do sequentially.
